newsitem.title: USA: Paul Harris Q2 expenses decline.
newsitem.headline: Paul Harris Q2 expenses decline.

text.p: Paul Harris Stores Inc, a specialty retailer of private-label women's casual wear, said Monday that continued cost controls cut its second quarter selling, general and administrative expenses (SG&A) as a percentage of sales.
Earlier, Paul Harris reported earnings for the second quarter ended August 3 of $0.01 a share, compared with a year-ago loss of $0.08.
Second quarter sales rose to $36.7 million from $36.5 million. SG&A expenses fell to $11.4 million from $11.5 million.

Total inventory decreased by $1.4 million, while per-store inventory was up six percent. The company said per-store inventories rose due to an increase in accessories, which have proven to be extremely popular with customers.
Same store sales for the second quarter rose 13 percent.
The company said results for the second quarter were the best since 1989.
"Our earnings and (comparable) store sales in the quarter and first half show we continue to move in a positive direction," Charlotte Fischer, chairman, said in a statement.
She added the company has an upward trend in sales and is "optimistic" about its financials.

"As with any retailer, the second half will be critical for Paul Harris, and factors such as harsh winter weather or an unexpected downturn in the economy could have a negative effect on the important holiday season sales," Fischer said. "We feel that barring negative events that are out of our control, we are in a strong position to improve significantly compared with 1995's results."
In the fiscal year ended February 3, 1996, Paul Harris earned $0.16 a share.
